title: Effectiveness of professional toothbrushing on care home residents - a randomized controlled intervention study
summary: This randomized controlled intervention study aimed to explore that oral health of dement and non-dement care home residents (care level I-III) can be improved by professional toothbrushing performed by dental educated staff member as compared to care home residents without this intervention. Except for this intervention there will be no further changes in care routine.

interventions.name: Professional tooth cleaning of the care home residents at the begin of the study, furthermore one time instruction of the staff, participants receive a new toothbrush (Oral-B-CrossAction) and a new toothpaste (blendamed complete), professional toothbrushung is performed at an interval of 2 weeks by

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Care home residents St. Elizabeth, care level I-III, dement and non-dement, own consent of participate or consent of lawful deputy, at least 4 teeth left,
Exclusion criteria:
life-threatening illness or condition close to death, professional tooth cleaning at the begin of the study not possible according to health condition or dementia, forseeable loss of left tooth according to already diagnosed inflammation/ loosening of the teeth, toothless jaws, diabetes mellitus with HbA1c < 7.5, risk of endocarditis with necessary antibiotic screening prior to dental treatments, persons dependend on/ in employment contract with sponsor or examiner
